newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Crime sees SAfrica banks lose 113 mln rand last yr.
newsitem.headline: Crime sees SAfrica banks lose 113 mln rand last yr.

text.p: Robberies last year saw leading South African banks lose a total of 113 million rand ($25 million) Bob Tucker, chief executive of the Council of South African Banks (COSAB) said on Friday.

"South Africa's four major banks...also announced today that this figure is approximately one fifth of the total cost of their securing branches, automatic teller machines and cash in transit," Tucker told a news briefing.
The country's leading banks are Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd, First National Bank Holdings Ltd, Nedcor Ltd and Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd.
South Africa recently experienced a renewed wave of violent crime, with high-profile car hijackings and a continued assault on banks and foreign exchange bureaus in the limelight in the past month.
Last week top economist Ronnie Bethlehem was slain at his house in a car hijacking.
The country's bank robbery statistics rate among the highest in the world, Tucker said. Only 1.1 million rand was lost in bank robberies in Britain during 1996.
He said the number of reported robberies among the above banks increased from 268 in 1995 to 316 last year, and the total monetary loss increased by 38 percent.

"The cost of cash is fast becoming so great that individual banks are likely to take steps to recoup some of the costs of providing cash. In the longer term, alternatives to cash must be sought," Tucker said.
Attacks were not only restricted to banks but South African businesses across the spectrum were suffering.
"Losses reported by banks are probably only a fraction of the total losses suffered by the business community."

The four main banks would spend up to one billion rand on crime prevention and security measures until the end of 1997 in an attempt to stem the tide of violent robberies, but it would ultimately be up to government to deal with the problem, Tucker said.
